metadata.title: Geno Smith - Tosses three TDs in Week 11 win
metadata.description: Smith completed 17 of 21 passes for 176 yards and three touchdowns in Sunday's 27-24 win over the Chargers. He also rushed once for four yards.
metadata.analysis: Smith didn't have a completion longer than 21 yards but kept the offense on schedule with an accurate performance. Most importantly, he stepped up in the red zone, which has been the team's Achilles' heel throughout the season. Smith threw a seven-yard touchdown pass to Breece Hall to snap the Jets' two-game touchdown drought in the second quarter, then tacked on touchdown passes of eight and 15 yards to practice squad elevation Sterling Shepard. The veteran QB will take a 15:3 TD:INT into a Week 12 road game against the Dolphins, who defeated the Jets in Week 7 despite three touchdown passes from Smith.

metadata.title: Geno Smith Set to Start With Superflex Appeal in Week 11
metadata.description: New York Jets quarterback Geno Smith (ankle) practiced in full Friday after being limited Thursday and listed as limited on Wednesday's estimated report. He carries no injury designation and will start Sunday against the Los Angeles Chargers. Smith completed 13 of 21 passes for 148 yards before leaving last week's loss to Buffalo. He threw for 165 yards at Kansas City the week before, and the Jets went without a touchdown in both games. RotoBaller ranks him QB20 for Week 11, putting him in play as a second quarterback in Superflex. Los Angeles gave up 340 passing yards to Jacoby Brissett on Monday, though he needed 49 attempts and threw no touchdowns. According to the Jets, Smith has completed 48% of his passes that traveled at least 20 yards in the air, the sixth-best rate in the NFL. His last multi-touchdown game came in Week 8, when he threw for 290 yards against Las Vegas. Those downfield completions can lift his yardage even if New York keeps converting red-zone trips into touchdowns at its league-low rate of 37.9%.

metadata.title: Geno Smith - Cleared to play Week 11
metadata.description: Smith (ankle) doesn't have an injury designation for Sunday's game against the Chargers.
metadata.analysis: Smith dealt with an ankle injury during the week after he was forced from last Sunday's loss against the Bills, but all scans came back clean, and the veteran quarterback is good to go for a road date in Los Angeles. Smith has been able to get the ball to his playmakers this season, but he doesn't have any fantasy upside as a statuesque pocket passer in an offense that likes to run the ball.

metadata.title: Geno Smith has No Designation, Will Play Sunday
metadata.description: New York Jets quarterback Geno Smith (ankle) has no injury designation for the Week 11 contest and will play on Sunday on the road against the Los Angeles Chargers, according to Zack Rosenblatt of The Athletic. Smith suffered an ankle injury and was tested for a concussion in Sunday's Week 10 loss to the division-rival Buffalo Bills, but the 36-year-old veteran avoided any serious injuries and is in the clear to play this weekend as the Jets look to end their lengthy losing streak. While Smith has looked much better than he did in his disastrous 2025 campaign with the Las Vegas Raiders, he still profiles as a low-end QB2 in superflex fantasy leagues, and he will be without rookie first-round receiver Omar Cooper Jr. (ankle). The two-time Pro Bowler has completed 67.1% of his passes for 2,226 yards, 12 touchdowns, and only three interceptions in 10 starts after tossing a league-high 17 picks last year. He had a nice two-game stretch in Weeks 7 and 8 against the Miami Dolphins and Raiders, where he threw for 577 yards, five TDs, and only two interceptions. But in the last two games against the Bills and Kansas City Chiefs, Smith has thrown for only 313 combined yards, zero touchdowns, and zero interceptions. With potential limited mobility against a Chargers defense that is around the middle of the pack in terms of fantasy points allowed to QBs this year, Smith has limited upside, with potential limited mobility outside of the pocket.

metadata.title: Geno Smith (ankle) practicing in full Friday
metadata.description: Geno Smith (ankle) will practice in full on Friday.
metadata.analysis: Smith was a limited participant at Thursday's practice session and will get in even more activity Friday. This suggests the veteran QB should be good to go for Sunday's matchup with the Chargers.

metadata.title: Geno Smith - Looking good for Week 11
metadata.description: Smith (ankle) will practice Friday, and head coach Aaron Glenn said "things look promising for him playing Sunday," Brian Costello of the New York Post reports.
metadata.analysis: While the initial report indicated only that Smith would practice, Eric Allen of the Jets' official website reported that Smith will be a full participant Friday, which makes it even more likely that he will be under center in Week 11. The Jets' final injury report will reveal whether or not Smith carries an injury designation into Sunday's game against the Chargers.

metadata.title: Geno Smith to Practice in Full Friday, Trending Towards Playing Sunday
metadata.description: New York Jets quarterback Geno Smith (ankle) will practice in full on Friday and is trending toward being available for his team's Week 11 matchup against the Los Angeles Chargers, per ESPN's Rich Cimini. Smith suffered an ankle injury during New York's Week 10 loss to the Buffalo Bills that forced him to exit the game early, but it appears the veteran quarterback has avoided a serious issue. Across 10 games in 2026, Smith has completed 67.1% of his pass attempts for 2,226 yards, 12 touchdowns, and three interceptions. The Jets have a potentially higher-upside option behind Smith in fourth-round rookie Cade Klubnik, who completed 11 of 20 pass attempts for 137 yards and an interception in relief of Smith against Buffalo. However, Smith is a safer option who provides more stability for Jets wide receiver Garrett Wilson.

metadata.title: Geno Smith (ankle) limited in practice Thursday
metadata.description: Geno Smith was limited in practice on Thursday.
metadata.analysis: Smith has logged back-to-back limited practices. He is trending towards being good to go for Sunday's game against the Chargers.

metadata.title: Geno Smith - Remains limited Thursday
metadata.description: Smith (ankle) was a limited participant in Thursday's practice.
metadata.analysis: Smith was also deemed limited on Wednesday's practice estimate, so he may need to work fully Friday in order to approach Sunday's game against the Chargers without an injury designation. For his part, the Jets' QB1 isn't worried about his Week 11 availability, with ESPN's Rich Cimini noting Wednesday that while Smith still was walking with a noticeable limp at that point, the signal caller stated that he intends to play this weekend." That's the plan," Smith said. "Obviously, you've got to take it day by day, but that's the plan."

metadata.title: Geno Smith Limited Again on Thursday
metadata.description: New York Jets quarterback Geno Smith (ankle) was listed as a limited participant in practice for the second straight day on Thursday due to an ankle injury that knocked him out of Sunday's Week 10 loss to the division-rival Buffalo Bills. Smith was also evaluated for a concussion in the same game, but tests on Monday ruled out any significant injuries for the 36-year-old veteran signal-caller. Smith said the plan is for him to start on Sunday on the road against the Los Angeles Chargers, although he might be a little limited mobility-wise if his ankle is not 100%. After a two-week stretch against the division-rival Miami Dolphins and Las Vegas Raiders in which he threw five touchdown passes, Smith and the Jets' offense has been in a rut the last two weeks, with Smith failing to top 200 yards passing in either game without a single touchdown pass. The Jets will be facing the one-win Chargers on the road, which will be a great chance for them to snap their long losing streak, but the Chargers' defense has not been a slam-dunk matchup for opposing QBs this year, and a banged-up Smith should not be considered anything more than a low-end QB2 option for fantasy managers in two-QB superflex leagues. He could be without impressive rookie receiver Omar Cooper Jr. (ankle), too, after he aggravated an ongoing ankle injury last week.

metadata.title: Geno Smith - Limited, but plans to play Sunday
metadata.description: Smith (ankle), who was a limited participant in Wednesday's walkthrough practice, said afterward that he intends to play in Sunday's game against the Chargers, Rich Cimini of ESPN.com reports.
metadata.analysis: Beyond noting that Smith will start if healthy, head coach Aaron Glenn hasn't confirmed that Smith will be available this weekend, but the quarterback's ability to practice in some capacity Wednesday is at least an encouraging sign for his status. Cimini notes that Smith was walking with a noticeable limp three days after injuring his left ankle in a Week 10 loss to the Bills, so the veteran signal-caller's mobility could be compromised to some degree if he gets the green light to play against the Chargers. Rookie Cade Klubnik would be in line for his first NFL start in the event Smith isn't deemed healthy enough to play this weekend.

metadata.title: Geno Smith (ankle) limited on Wednesday
metadata.description: Geno Smith (ankle) gets in limited action at Wednesday's practice.
metadata.analysis: Smith is dealing with an ankle injury that took him out of this past Sunday's game early. The issue is not severe, however, and the veteran QB was at least able to get in some activity Wednesday. Rookie Cade Klubnik would be in line to start if Smith ultimately cannot go in Week 11.

metadata.title: Geno Smith - Opening Week 11 with limited practice
metadata.description: Jets head coach Aaron Glenn said that Smith (ankle) will be a limited participant in Wednesday's practice, Brian Costello of the New York Post reports.
metadata.analysis: Smith was unable to return to this past Sunday's 31-12 loss to the Bills after tweaking his left ankle in the third quarter, but medical tests conducted after the game revealed no major injury. The veteran signal-caller will still be operating with a cap on his reps to begin Week 11 prep, and Glenn acknowledged that the Jets will wait and see how Smith fares as the week rolls along before a decision is made on his status for Sunday's game against the Chargers. Rookie Cade Klubnik would be in line to start in Los Angeles if Smith isn't cleared to play.

metadata.title: Teammate Says Geno Smith is "Good to Go"
metadata.description: New York Jets wide receiver Garrett Wilson believes that veteran quarterback Geno Smith (ankle) will play this weekend in Los Angeles against the Chargers, according to Rich Cimini of ESPN. "From what I know, Geno feels good to go. You would have to ask him. From what I know, he's good to go. So I'll say that," Wilson said on Smith's status. Smith was checked for a concussion in Sunday's loss to the division-rival Buffalo Bills before eventually being knocked out of the contest with an ankle injury. The 36-year-old is set for a limited practice on Wednesday, though, and all signs are pointing to him starting in Week 11 against the Chargers after tests earlier this week ruled out any significant injuries. He is still walking with a slight limp, but he expects to play on Sunday. Smith threw five touchdowns in Weeks 7 and 8 against the division-rival Miami Dolphins and Las Vegas Raiders, throwing for a combined 577 yards, but in the last two weeks, he has thrown for only 313 yards with no touchdowns or interceptions against the Bills and Kansas City Chiefs. The veteran signal-caller has looked much better than he did in his disastrous season last year in Vegas, but he should still not be considered much more than a low-end QB2 streamer in superflex leagues against the Chargers if he is active.

metadata.title: Geno Smith to be Limited in Wednesday's Practice
metadata.description: New York Jets quarterback Geno Smith (ankle) will be limited in Wednesday's practice, head coach Aaron Glenn told Rich Cimini of ESPN. Smith was beat up in Sunday's Week 10 loss to the division-rival Buffalo Bills, getting knocked out of the game with an ankle injury while also being checked for a concussion after taking a hard hit. Tests on Monday cleared the 36-year-old veteran of any significant injuries, which means he is on the right side of questionable as the Jets prepare for the Los Angeles Chargers on the road this Sunday in Week 11. Smith was not a full practice participant to begin the week, but as long as he does not have any setbacks with his ankle this week, he should start under center as the Jets look to put an end to their losing streak. The 13-year veteran and two-time Pro Bowler has been better in 2026 than he was when he led the league with 17 interceptions with the Las Vegas Raiders last year, but he is still nothing more than a low-end QB2 option for fantasy managers in superflex leagues, and that will not change if he is available to play in L.A. this weekend. After throwing five touchdowns in two games against the Miami Dolphins and Raiders, Smith has been under 200 yards passing in each of the last two games against the Bills and Kansas City Chiefs without throwing a touchdown or an interception.

metadata.title: Geno Smith (ankle) avoids major injury
metadata.description: Geno Smith underwent tests on Monday that did not reveal anything major.
metadata.analysis: Smith will continue to be evaluated through the week. He will have a chance to be ready to go for Week 11.

metadata.title: Geno Smith - Undergoes tests on ankle
metadata.description: Smith (ankle) underwent tests Monday that did not reveal any major injuries, but he will continue to be evaluated during the week, Ian Rapoport of NFL Network reports.
metadata.analysis: Smith was checked for a concussion in Sunday's loss to the Bills but was cleared and returned to the game before then suffering an ankle injury. He finished the game 13 of 21 passing for 148 yards and no touchdowns or interceptions. It sounds like Smith has a good chance to suit up next Sunday against the Chargers, but if he's not cleared, then rookie Cade Klubnik would be in line to make the start.

metadata.title: Geno Smith's Tests Reveal No Major Injuries
metadata.description: New York Jets quarterback Geno Smith (ankle), who dealt with ankle and head injuries in the team's Week 10 loss to the Buffalo Bills on Sunday, underwent tests on Monday that did not reveal anything major, sources told Ian Rapoport of the NFL Network. Smith, whose ankle is the biggest concern, will continue to be evaluated through the week, but so far, everything looks good. The 36-year-old took a hard hit against Buffalo and was evaluated for a concussion on Sunday before eventually returning, only to injure his ankle and be ruled out for the rest of the contest. He finished the day 13-for-21 passing for just 148 yards with no touchdowns or interceptions. Head coach Aaron Glenn told the media on Monday that if Smith is cleared later this week of any physical issues, he will make the start on Sunday on the road in Los Angeles against the Chargers in Week 11. Rookie Cade Klubnik saw the first snaps of his NFL career against Buffalo and initially gave the offense a little jolt with his legs, but he ultimately finished 11-for-20 passing for 137 yards, no touchdowns, and one interception. The Jets will stick with Smith, who has looked much better in 2026 than he did with the Las Vegas Raiders in 2025, if he is healthy. If Smith is active against the Chargers, he will continue to be a midrange QB2 option for fantasy managers this weekend against a Chargers defense that has been middle of the pack in terms of fantasy points allowed to opposing signal-callers.

metadata.title: Geno Smith (ankle) to undergo MRI Monday
metadata.description: Jets head coach Aaron Glenn said Geno Smith will undergo an MRI on Monday.
metadata.analysis: Smith left Sunday's game early against the Bills with an ankle injury. There should be an update on his status later this week.

metadata.title: Geno Smith - Set for MRI on ankle
metadata.description: Jets head coach Aaron Glenn said that Smith will get further imaging on his left ankle Monday, Antwan V. Staley of the New York Daily News reports.
metadata.analysis: Glenn said that he won't have an update on Smith's status until later in the week once his MRI results are read, but the coach noted that Smith -- if healthy -- will remain the Jets' starting quarterback heading into next Sunday's game against the Chargers. Smith played less than half of the Jets' offensive snaps in this past Sunday's 31-12 loss to the Bills, missing time while getting checked for a concussion and then due to the ankle injury. Backup Cade Klubnik finished out the game under center in place of Smith, who completed 13 of 21 throws for 148 yards before exiting for good in the third quarter.

metadata.title: Geno Smith Will Remain Jets Starter if Healthy
metadata.description: New York Jets head coach Aaron Glenn said that quarterback Geno Smith (ankle) will remain the team's starting quarterback if he's healthy. Smith suffered an ankle injury in the 31-12 loss to the Buffalo Bills and didn't return, prompting rookie Cade Klubnik to enter the lineup. Klubnik completed 11 of 20 passes for 137 yards and one interception, and added three carries for 26 yards on the ground. With Smith set to remain the Jets' starting quarterback, his health is a major question, as he's scheduled to undergo an MRI on his ankle. Glenn wouldn't speculate on his game status for Week 11's matchup against the Los Angeles Chargers, but if he misses time, Klubnik would start in his place. Fantasy managers in SuperFlex leagues should keep an eye on Smith's status, as his absence could open the door for the rookie quarterback, who would be a top waiver option in Week 11.

metadata.title: Geno Smith - Status for Week 11 uncertain
metadata.description: Jets head coach Aaron Glenn said after Sunday's loss to Buffalo that Smith, who departed the contest due to an ankle injury, will have his status for Week 11 determined during the upcoming week of practice, Jack Bell of the Jets' official site reports.
metadata.analysis: Smith was hurt during New York's final offensive series of the first half Sunday when he was hit by a pair of defenders while throwing an incomplete pass. He was placed in concussion protocol and passed, clearing the way for him to return to the game. However, Smith then exited again after hurting his ankle, and this time he was unable to return. The veteran quarterback's practice activity, if any, during Week 11 prep will likely determine if he's able to suit up next Sunday against the Chargers. If Smith can't play, rookie Cade Klubnik would likely start under center.

metadata.title: Geno Smith (ankle) exits Sunday's game early
metadata.description: Geno Smith (ankle) exited Sunday's gam early and did not return. He completed 13-of-21 passes for 148 yards prior to his injury.
metadata.analysis: Smith also exited the game to be evaluated for a concussion, but returned briefly before suffering an ankle injury. Fantasy managers will want to monitor his status ahead of a Week 11 game with the Chargers.

metadata.title: Geno Smith - Won't finish Sunday's game
metadata.description: Smith (ankle) has been ruled out for the remainder of Sunday's game against the Bills, Brian Costello of the New York Post reports.
metadata.analysis: After previously exiting the contest and then clearing the NFL's concussion protocol, Smith is now done for the day with an ankle issue after completing 13 of 21 pass attempts for 148 yards. Once again, Cade Klubnik has been summoned to fill in for Smith, whose status will need to be closely monitored as next Sunday's game against the Chargers approaches.

metadata.title: Geno Smith - Hurts ankle Sunday
metadata.description: Smith headed to the medical tent during Sunday's game against the Bills after injuring his ankle,  Rich Cimini of ESPN.com reports.
metadata.analysis: Smith, who previously exited the game to be checked for a head injury and subsequently cleared the NFL's concussion protocol and returned to the field, but now an ankle issue has him deemed questionable to resume action by the Jets. As a result, Cade Klubnik is back in at QB for New York.

metadata.title: Geno Smith - Back in Sunday's game
metadata.description: Smith has cleared the NFL's concussion protocol and has returned to Sunday's game against the Bills, Ian Rapoport of NFL Network and ESPN reports.
metadata.analysis: Smith previously exited the contest and headed to the blue medical tent after absorbing a hard hit, but after being checked out he's back in there at QB for the Jets. While Smith was sidelined, Cade Klubnik subbed in for him, completing two of four passes for 39 yards and rushing twice for 19 yards.

metadata.title: Geno Smith being evaluated for a concussion
metadata.description: Jets QB Geno Smith is currently being evaluated for a concussion.
metadata.analysis: Smith was hit hard ending the second quarter. Cade Klubnik is currently in at quarterback for the Jets.

metadata.title: Geno Smith - Heads to medical tent Sunday
metadata.description: Smith exited Sunday's game against the Bills and headed to the blue medical tent after absorbing a hard hit, Connor Hughes of SNY reports.
metadata.analysis: Prior to that, Smith completed nine of 16 passes for 113 yards. It remains to be seen if the QB is back out there for second half of the contest, but on the plus side, Hughes notes that Smith subsequently returned to the team's bench as opposed to going to the locker room.

metadata.title: Geno Smith Ruled Out With Ankle Injury
metadata.description: New York Jets quarterback Geno Smith (ankle) has been ruled out for the remainder of Sunday's home game against the Buffalo Bills. Smith, 36, did not start the second half after taking a hard hit at the end of the second quarter. He briefly returned in the third after clearing concussion protocol, but limped back to the medical tent after one drive. The veteran completed 13 of 21 passes for 148 yards and no touchdowns before exiting Sunday's game. Rookie quarterback Cade Klubnik, who had only played in the season opener, took over for Smith to start the second half and remains in the game.

metadata.title: Geno Smith Questionable to Return with Ankle  Injury
metadata.description: New York Jets quarterback Geno Smith (ankle) is questionable to return to Sunday's game against the Buffalo Bills with an apparent ankle injury. The 36-year-old veteran previously exited the Week 10 matchup after taking a hard hit at the end of the first half. He briefly returned in the third quarter after clearing concussion protocol, but was seen limping back to the medical tent after one drive and subsequently went to the locker room. Smith completed 13 of 21 pass attempts for 148 yards before exiting the game. Rookie quarterback Cade Klubnik started the second half for Smith and is playing in just his second game of the season.

metadata.title: Geno Smith Back in Medical Tent vs. Bills
metadata.description: New York Jets quarterback Geno Smith (undisclosed) went back to the medical tent in the third quarter of his team's Week 10 matchup against the Buffalo Bills. The 36-year-old veteran previously went to the tent after a hit late in the first half of Sunday's home game, and he briefly returned in the third quarter after clearing concussion protocol. Smith completed 11 of 18 passes for 145 yards before going into the tent a second time. Rookie quarterback Cade Klubnik started the second half, completing two of four passes for 39 yards before Smith briefly returned.

metadata.title: Geno Smith Goes to Medical Tent After Late First-Half Hit
metadata.description: New York Jets quarterback Geno Smith went to the medical tent after taking a hit on a third-down incompletion with 25 seconds left in the first half of Sunday's Week 10 game against the Buffalo Bills. Trainers helped Smith off the field, and he returned to the bench before halftime, according to Zack Rosenblatt. Smith completed nine of 16 passes for 113 yards with no touchdowns or interceptions. He took one sack before leaving. Rookie quarterback Cade Klubnik replaced Smith, who is being evaluated for a concussion.

metadata.title: Geno Smith Is Best Suited for Superflex Leagues Against Buffalo
metadata.description: New York Jets quarterback Geno Smith was sacked five times for a loss of 42 yards at Kansas City, where his longest completion went for 19 yards. New York has allowed 28 sacks in nine games. Buffalo held Minnesota without a third-down conversion on eight attempts last week, though the Bills have allowed 15 passing touchdowns in eight games. Smith has a better chance to test that secondary downfield if Garrett Wilson (concussion) plays. Wilson was limited Thursday, practiced fully Friday and is questionable. Smith has completed nine passes of at least 40 yards this season, but he threw for just 165 yards and no touchdowns without Wilson in Week 9. RotoBaller ranks Smith QB16 for Week 10. He fits as a Superflex starter, particularly if he gets his leading receiver back. Smith has rushed for 54 yards without a touchdown through nine games. Buffalo kept Minnesota out of the end zone last week and intercepted two passes. With little rushing production to offset a quiet passing day, Smith is a sit in typical one-quarterback leagues.

metadata.title: Geno Smith Has Week 10 Streaming Appeal
metadata.description: New York Jets quarterback Geno Smith draws a Buffalo defense that allowed 15 passing touchdowns through its first seven games. Smith threw for 577 yards and five touchdowns against Miami and Las Vegas before struggling in last Sunday's loss to Kansas City. He finished with just 165 passing yards, playing without Garrett Wilson (concussion), who remains uncertain for Week 10. Buffalo has faced more than 38 pass attempts per game this season, giving Smith a chance to rebound if the Jets are forced to throw frequently. Wilson's availability will be important when evaluating Smith for Sunday's matchup. Available in most fantasy leagues, Smith is a potential one-week streaming option, especially if Wilson returns to the lineup.

metadata.title: Geno Smith - No TDs in Week 9 loss
metadata.description: Smith completed 18 of 32 passes for 165 yards, no touchdowns and no interceptions in Sunday's 35-12 loss to the Chiefs. He also rushed once for eight yards.
metadata.analysis: Smith struggled in the absence of top wide receiver Garrett Wilson (concussion), as the Jets made four field goals in the first half before getting blanked in the second half. The veteran QB posted his second-lowest total of the season for passing yards and was held without a touchdown for the first time since Week 1. Smith could be busy in Week 10 with the 2-7 Jets likely to be forced into a pass-heavy game plan if they fall behind against the Bills.

metadata.title: Geno Smith held in check in Week 9 loss
metadata.description: Geno Smith completed 18-of-32 pass attempts for 165 yards in a 35-12 loss to the Jets. He added eight rushing yards on one carry.
metadata.analysis: Smith and the Jets' offense failed to get anything consistent going, stalling out and having to settle for field goals in their scoring chances. This did break a streak of seven straight games with at least one passing touchdown for the veteran. Smith and the Jets will take on the Bills in Week 10.

metadata.title: Geno Smith Loses Top Target Ahead of Week 9
metadata.description: New York Jets quarterback Geno Smith will face the Kansas City Chiefs on Sunday without Garrett Wilson (concussion), who leads the team with 43 catches and 527 receiving yards. Smith threw for 290 yards and 2 touchdowns against Las Vegas in Week 8, averaging 9.1 yards per attempt. The Jets have scored 25 and 33 points over their last two games, and Smith has thrown 12 touchdown passes against 3 interceptions this season. His 15 completions on passes traveling at least 20 yards in the air are tied for the league lead. Adonai Mitchell, coming off a 142-yard game, gives Smith another receiver who can win downfield. Kansas City has allowed 7 passing touchdowns in seven games, though Bo Nix accounted for 2 of them on 222 passing yards last Sunday. Smith has rushed for just 46 yards without a touchdown in eight games, so replacing Wilson's production matters even more to his fantasy outlook. He is a low-end QB2 for Superflex managers and a sit in 12-team, one-quarterback leagues.

metadata.title: Geno Smith Becoming a Viable Streaming Option Once Again
metadata.description: New York Jets quarterback Geno Smith had another strong fantasy performance in Sunday's loss to the Las Vegas Raiders, throwing for 290 yards, two touchdowns, and one interception. Geno has now surpassed 250 passing yards in three consecutive games, throwing for 829 yards, six touchdowns, and three interceptions over that time. It's not perfect, but it never is with Geno, and after a truly embarrassing 2025 season with the Raiders, he is once again a usable, matchup-dependent streaming option. While he shouldn't be streamed with much confidence in his Week 9 matchup against Kansas City, his schedule after that becomes much more playable, squaring off against the Bills, Chargers, and Dolphins, followed by their bye in Week 13. Geno is worth a roster spot in deeper leagues, but fantasy managers should remain selective about when they actually trust him in their starting lineups.

metadata.title: Geno Smith tosses late interception in Week 8 loss
metadata.description: Geno Smith completed 20-of-32 passes for 290 yards, two touchdowns, and one interception in a 38-33 loss to the Jets. He added four rushing yards on one carry.
metadata.analysis: Smith found Adonai Mitchell and Isaiah Williams in the second quarter to account for his two touchdown passes. Smith has struggled with the turnovers as of late, tossing an interception in three straight games. Smith and the Jets will take on the Chiefs in Week 9.

metadata.title: Geno Smith - Late INT seals sixth loss
metadata.description: Smith completed 20 of 32 passes for 290 yards, two touchdowns and one interception in Sunday's 38-33 loss to the Raiders. He also rushed once for four yards.
metadata.analysis: Smith threw second-quarter touchdown passes of 18 yards to Isaiah Williams and 12 yards to Adonai Mitchell while coming 10 yards shy of his second 300-yard passing performance of the season. The veteran QB had a chance to orchestrate a game-winning drive against his former team, but the Jets' comeback bid came up short when Smith threw an end-zone interception from the Raiders' 35-yard line with seven seconds remaining. Smith has been picked off in each of his last three outings after going without an interception through five starts to open his second tenure with the Jets. He'll take a 12:3 TD:INT into a Week 9 trip to Kansas City.

metadata.title: Geno Smith Offers QB2 Value Against Struggling Raiders Defense
metadata.description: New York Jets quarterback Geno Smith has a favorable opportunity against his former team when the Las Vegas Raiders visit in Week 8. Las Vegas ranks 29th in total defense, allowing 373.7 yards per game, and gave up three touchdown passes to Matthew Stafford last week despite holding him to 195 passing yards. Smith is coming off 287 yards and three touchdowns against Miami, with Omar Cooper Jr.'s emergence giving him an explosive option beyond Garrett Wilson. Smith has completed 70.0% of his passes at 7.8 yards per attempt this season, with 10 touchdowns against two interceptions. That efficiency supports his QB19 ranking at RotoBaller and makes him a useful Superflex starter. New York's protection has been less consistent, allowing 21 sacks, although right tackle Armand Membou has surrendered only three pressures within 2.5 seconds of the snap all season, according to Next Gen Stats. Smith's limited rushing contribution, just 42 yards without a touchdown, leaves him dependent on passing production. Smith has averaged 29.6 pass attempts per game, so his efficient passing has come on modest volume, limiting his appeal as a one-quarterback streamer.

metadata.title: Geno Smith Is a Week 8 Streamer Against the Raiders
metadata.description: New York Jets quarterback Geno Smith is a Week 8 streamer in leagues with at least 14 teams, and the matchup is the whole case. He threw three touchdown passes for the second time this season in Sunday's 28-25 loss to the Miami Dolphins, completing 23 of 30 attempts for 287 yards and one interception, with two touchdowns to Mason Taylor and one to Omar Cooper Jr. The rookie receiver has now surpassed 100 yards in consecutive games, giving Smith another productive weapon alongside Garrett Wilson. However, Smith threw just one touchdown in each of the three games between his three-score performances against the Detroit Lions and Miami, and his 42 rushing yards through seven starts offer little additional fantasy production. The Jets host a Las Vegas Raiders defense that has surrendered 16 passing touchdowns, tied for the second-most in the NFL, and the Kansas City Chiefs and Buffalo Bills await New York in the following two weeks, so add him.

metadata.title: Geno Smith tosses three touchdowns in Week 7 loss
metadata.description: Geno Smith completed 23-of-30 passes for 287 yards, three touchdowns, and one interception in a 28-25 loss to Miami.
metadata.analysis: Smith and the Jets trailed the Dolphins, allowing for a high volume passing attack in the final three quarters. Smith connected with Mason Taylor twice and Omar Cooper for his three touchdown passes. Smith and the Jets will take on the Raiders in Week 8.

metadata.title: Geno Smith - Three TDs not enough in Week 7
metadata.description: Smith completed 23 of 30 passes for 287 yards, three touchdowns and one interception in Sunday's 28-25 loss to the Dolphins. He also rushed twice for no gain and threw a successful two-point conversion.
metadata.analysis: Smith matched Miami's opening-drive touchdown with a 13-yard touchdown pass to Mason Taylor on the Jets' first drive, but the veteran QB threw an interception deep in Dolphins territory on the next drive. The Jets trailed for the entirety of the last three quarters, allowing Smith to rack up some big numbers during their failed comeback bid, as he posted his second three-touchdown performance of the season. He found Omar Cooper for a three-yard touchdown in the third quarter after they connected for a 60-yard gain earlier on that drive, and Smith threw a 12-yard touchdown and two-point conversion, both to Taylor, to round out the scoring with 3:24 remaining in the fourth, but the Dolphins ran out the clock from there to drop the Jets to 2-5 heading into a Week 8 home game against the Raiders.

metadata.title: Geno Smith Offers Week 7 Streaming Appeal Against Miami
metadata.description: New York Jets quarterback Geno Smith is a QB2 and streaming consideration in deeper one-quarterback leagues because the Miami Dolphins, visiting Sunday, have converted an NFL-low 8.2% of their pressures into sacks, while Smith has faced pressure on 42.7% of his dropbacks. He completed 20 of 30 passes for 252 yards, a touchdown, and an interception against the New England Patriots in Week 6, bringing his season totals to 1,336 passing yards, seven touchdowns, and one interception with a 68.9% completion rate. Adonai Mitchell's return gives him another receiving option alongside Garrett Wilson and Omar Cooper Jr. He has thrown multiple touchdown passes only once this season and has contributed just 42 rushing yards.

metadata.title: Geno Smith has Put Himself on the QB2 Streaming Radar
metadata.description: New York Jets veteran quarterback Geno Smith is playing much better than he did last year with the Las Vegas Raiders. In his first six games with the Jets, the two-time Pro Bowler has completed 68.9% of his 177 pass attempts for 1,336 yards, seven touchdowns, and only one interception. The lack of interceptions is particularly noteworthy after Smith tossed a league-high 17 picks in 15 starts for the Raiders in his lone year in Sin City. The 36-year-old went 20-for-30 for 252 yards, one touchdown, and one interception in Sunday's 26-19 Week 6 loss to the division-rival New England Patriots. Smith did not have eye-popping numbers, but he was impressive nevertheless and brought the Jets back in the second half to make things interesting. It has helped his cause that rookie first-round receiver Omar Cooper Jr. is back from Injured Reserve. Cooper caught six passes for 103 yards and a touchdown against the Pats in his first game back. Going into a Week 7 divisional contest against the winless Miami Dolphins, Smith is an attractive QB2 streamer in superflex leagues. He is the QB19 in overall fantasy points early in the season.

metadata.title: Geno Smith - Solid numbers despite loss
metadata.description: Smith completed 20 of 30 passes for 252 yards with one touchdown and one interception while adding two rushes for minus-1 yard in the Jets' 26-19 loss to the Patriots on Sunday.
metadata.analysis: Smith took three sacks while trying to play catch-up all afternoon, and in that context, his final numbers were all the more impressive. The veteran signal-caller helped the Jets claw back from a 17-3 halftime deficit to get within four entering the fourth quarter, but his interception at the Patriots' 24-yard line early in the period snuffed out a potential scoring opportunity. Smith has certainly given New York some much-needed veteran stability at the quarterback position and displayed encouraging chemistry with returning rookie Omar Cooper (6-103-1) on Sunday, so there's reason for optimism heading into a favorable Week 7 home matchup against the Dolphins on Sunday.

metadata.title: Geno Smith tosses one touchdown in Week 6 loss
metadata.description: Geno Smith completed 20-of-30 pass attempts for 252 yards, one touchdown, and one interception in a 26-19 loss to the Patriots.
metadata.analysis: Smith connected with Omar Cooper Jr. on a deep pass for the Jets' lone passing touchdown of the day. Smith spread the ball around effectively and was intercepted for the first time this season. The Jets and Smith will take on Miami at home in Week 7.

metadata.title: Geno Smith Difficult to Trust Against New England
metadata.description: New York Jets quarterback Geno Smith has completed 69.4% of his passes for 1,084 yards, six touchdowns, and no interceptions through five games, but those numbers have not translated into consistently useful fantasy performances. He managed only 182 passing yards and one touchdown against Cleveland in Week 5, marking his second consecutive outing below 200 yards. Protection remains another concern, with Smith already taking 16 sacks this season. The Jets now travel to New England to face a Patriots defense coming off an impressive performance against Las Vegas, which managed just 17 points in Week 5. Smith's connection with Garrett Wilson provides some upside, but New York has not generated enough offensive production to support dependable quarterback scoring. RotoBaller ranks Smith QB28 for Week 6, leaving him outside the starting conversation in conventional one-quarterback leagues. Even in superflex formats, he profiles as a lower-end option.

metadata.title: Geno Smith Offers Limited Waiver Appeal Ahead of Week 6
metadata.description: New York Jets quarterback Geno Smith is worth rostering as depth in Superflex and two-quarterback leagues, but he is difficult to justify as a Week 6 pickup in standard one-QB formats. Smith completed 17 of 30 passes for 182 yards and a touchdown in Sunday's 17-12 win over Cleveland, marking his second consecutive outing below 200 passing yards. He has totaled just 301 yards and two touchdowns over those two games after throwing for 321 yards and three scores against Detroit in Week 3. Through five starts, the 36-year-old has completed 69.4% of his passes for 1,084 yards, six touchdowns, and no interceptions. However, he has also taken 16 sacks while contributing only 43 rushing yards, leaving him heavily dependent on passing production. The Jets travel to New England in Week 6 to face a Patriots defense ranked fifth in total yards allowed and 10th against the pass. With New York averaging just 18.6 points per game and Smith exceeding 250 passing yards only once this season, fantasy managers in traditional one-quarterback leagues should leave him on the waiver wire.

metadata.title: Geno Smith - Modest numbers in rainy Week 5 win
metadata.description: Smith completed 17 of 30 pass attempts for 182 yards and a touchdown in Sunday's 17-12 win over the Browns. He also rushed five times for seven yards and lost a fumble.
metadata.analysis: Smith threw a 32-yard touchdown pass to Garrett Wilson on the team's first drive, but New York's passing game was quiet the rest of the way while playing through rainy conditions for the second time in as many home games. The veteran QB, who celebrated his 36th birthday Saturday, has a tidy 6:0 TD:INT, though Smith has put the ball on the ground in all but one game while losing two of four fumbles. Smith and the Jets will hope to get some of their injured skill position players back in Week 6 against the Patriots. Kenyon Sadiq (concussion) joined that growing list during Sunday's win.

metadata.title: Geno Smith throws TD in Week 5 win
metadata.description: Geno Smith completed 17 of his 30 passes for 182 yards and one touchdown while adding seven yards on five carries in a 17-12 win over the Browns in Week 5.
metadata.analysis: Smith struggled in rainy conditions at home in MetLife Stadium but he was still able to lead his team to the win. He lost a fumble on a strip-sack in the fourth quarter while his lone touchdown pass went to Garrett Wilson on a 32-yard connection in the first quarter. Smith has now thrown for six touchdowns and zero interceptions through five games. He will be on the QB2 radar in Week 6's road matchup against the Patriots.

metadata.title: Geno Smith Faces Another Difficult Matchup in Week 5
metadata.description: New York Jets quarterback Geno Smith is coming off a miserable afternoon against Chicago, completing eight of 15 passes for 119 yards and a touchdown in a game where the offense ran only 32 plays. Nearly half of his passing production came on a 58-yard touchdown to Isaiah Williams, and the Jets managed just 157 total yards. Things don't get much easier Sunday against Cleveland. The Browns have recorded at least three sacks in three straight games, including five against Pittsburgh last week, while Smith has been sacked 12 times over his last three appearances. New York will also be without Breece Hall and Adonai Mitchell again, further limiting its offensive options. Smith is QB26 in RotoBaller's Week 5 rankings. He's difficult to trust outside deeper two-quarterback and Superflex formats until the Jets show they can sustain drives consistently.

metadata.title: Geno Smith A Sneaky Waiver-Wire Target For Week 5
metadata.description: New York Jets quarterback Geno Smith threw for just 119 passing yards and one touchdown in Week 4, totaling under 8.8 PPR fantasy points just a week after dominating with 26.0 points. Smith's 14th season as an NFL QB has been a bumpy road, as at times he's looked like one of the NFL's better QBs and at other times like one of its worst. But he was missing his WR2, Adonai Mitchell (thumb) in Week 4. Mitchell is expected to be back in Week 5, and he was a huge part of the offense when he played. Having another legitimate threat as a separator across from WR Garrett Wilson, the team's WR1, helped the passing offense be much more productive, it seems. Week 4 also was a very odd game script for the Jets, as Smith attempted just 15 passes, of which he completed nine. His 7.9 yards per pass attempt was a very solid mark, it's just that he wasn't throwing the ball much. He attempted 41 and 37 passes in his previous two games, and a return to that volume at that efficiency rate would help him finish nicely in fantasy football. In deeper leagues, especially those with two quarterback spots or one superflex spot, Smith is a priority add if he's available on waivers.

metadata.title: Geno Smith struggles in loss to Bears
metadata.description: Geno Smith completed eight of his 15 passes for 119 yards and one touchdown in a 23-12 loss to the Bears in Week 4.
metadata.analysis: Smith took three sacks as the Jets struggled to get much going in what appeared to be a plus matchup against the Bears. Most of his damage came on a 58-yard touchdown pass to Isaiah Williams in the fourth quarter. Smith has now thrown five touchdowns and no interceptions through four games. He will be on the QB2 radar for fantasy heading into a Week 5 home matchup against the Browns.

metadata.title: Geno Smith - Just eight completions in loss
metadata.description: Smith completed eight of 15 pass attempts for 119 yards and a touchdown in Sunday's 23-12 loss to the Bears.
metadata.analysis: Smith threw for just 18 yards in the first half as the Jets took a 13-3 deficit into the locker room. Things didn't get much better offensively after halftime, except for Smith's 58-yard touchdown pass to Isaiah Williams in the fourth quarter. Smith has a 5:0 TD:INT and is averaging 226 passing yards heading into a Week 5 home game against the Browns.

metadata.title: Geno Smith Has Streaming Appeal in Week 4
metadata.description: New York Jets quarterback Geno Smith earned his way back onto the streaming radar with 321 yards and three touchdowns against Detroit. He completed 31 of 37 passes in that game and now has 783 yards, four touchdowns, and no interceptions through three weeks. The protection remains the part that can wreck the day. Smith was sacked five times by Detroit and has gone down nine times this season. Chicago just forced three turnovers while holding Philadelphia to seven points, so another clean 300-yard performance isn't something to assume. RotoBaller has Smith at QB19 for Week 4. He's playable if you're streaming the position and an easy Superflex start, but the offensive-line issues keep him outside the group of quarterbacks fantasy managers should feel obligated to use.

metadata.title: Geno Smith Among the Top Waiver-Wire Targets for Week 4
metadata.description: New York Jets quarterback Geno Smith has emerged as one of the most appealing waiver wire options heading into Week 4 of the NFL season. In a somewhat shocking turn of events, Smith racked up 321 passing yards and three passing touchdowns on Sunday, becoming the 15th-highest-scoring quarterback in fantasy football this year. This is a huge feat on its own, but it's even more impressive when you consider that Smith didn't have one of his favorite targets, Adonai Mitchell (finger). Maybe Smith won't rack up three touchdowns every game going forward, but he at least proved that he's capable of producing meaningful fantasy value while keeping the Jets in competitive games. The veteran quarterback could find himself in another high-scoring game against the Bears next week, vaulting him to the mid-range QB2 territory and making him one of the top quarterbacks to target on waivers.

metadata.title: Geno Smith tosses three touchdown in Week 3 loss
metadata.description: Geno Smith completed 31-of-37 passes for 321 yards and three touchdowns in a 31-24 loss to the Lions. He added 12 rushing yards on two carries.
metadata.analysis: Smith was excellent in a near upset of the Lions on the road. The veteran fumbled late in the fourth quarter, which allowed the Lions to seal the win. Smith was able to connect with Garrett Wilson, Kenyon Sadiq, and Jeremy Ruckert on his three touchdown passes. The Jets will head to Chicago to take on the Bears in Week 4.

metadata.title: Geno Smith - Tosses three TDs in Week 3 loss
metadata.description: Smith completed 31 of 37 passes for 321 yards and three touchdowns in Sunday's 31-24 loss to the Lions. He added 12 rushing yards on two carries and threw a two-point conversion.
metadata.analysis: The veteran QB was nearly flawless as the Jets nearly pulled off the upset, with his only turnover being a fumble on his fifth sack of the day late in the fourth quarter, ending his final possession. Smith spread the ball around, completing passes to eight different targets and connecting with Garrett Wilson, Jeremy Ruckert and rookie first-round pick Kenyon Sadiq for his scores. Smith has been extremely efficient to begin the season, posting a 75.5 percent completion rate (77-for-102) with a 4:0 TD:INT and 7.7 YPA. He'll look to stay sharp in a Week 4 road trip to Chicago.

metadata.title: Geno Smith Has Productive Day In Loss to Lions
metadata.description: New York Jets quarterback Geno Smith was very efficient and effective in the team's 31-24 loss to the Lions in Week 3. Smith was 31-for-37 passing for 321 passing yards and three touchdowns and added two carries for 12 rushing yards. It was a highly productive day for Smith, who found tight ends Kenyon Sadiq and Jeremy Ruckert for touchdown passes and also found his top receiver Garrett Wilson for a passing score. Smith took advantage of a fairly porous Lions defensive unit and had a great fantasy day. Look for Smith to continue his good season especially when receiver Adonai Mitchell returns from injury and adds another weapon to the passing attack.

metadata.title: Geno Smith Has Streaming Appeal Against Detroit
metadata.description: New York Jets quarterback Geno Smith threw for 247 yards and a touchdown in last week's overtime loss to Green Bay, completing 27 of 41 passes without an interception. He also added 17 rushing yards on five carries. The 41 attempts were a big jump from the 24 passes he threw in the opener, and Week 3 could require another busy afternoon. Detroit gave up 410 passing yards and three touchdowns to Tyler Shough in Week 1 before Josh Allen threw for 248 yards and three more scores last Thursday. Smith does not carry the same ceiling as Allen, but the matchup is much more inviting than the one he saw against Green Bay. RotoBaller ranks him as the QB18 for Week 3. He remains safest in Superflex leagues, though he also has some one-quarterback streaming appeal in Detroit.

metadata.title: High Volume Makes Geno Smith an Appealing Waiver-Wire Target
metadata.description: New York Jets quarterback Geno Smith is far from a flashy name in fantasy football, but his high passing volume and mistake-free streak put him on the radar as a solid waiver wire target. Smith threw 41 times in Week 2, completing 27 passes for 247 yards, one touchdown, and zero turnovers. He took four sacks, but he also logged 17 rushing yards. Smith has only one touchdown through two weeks, but it's also worth noting that he doesn't have any turnovers so far. He has been a steady presence at quarterback for the Jets, leading drives and supporting the fantasy stocks of Garrett Wilson and Breece Hall. Now, he's getting on the fantasy radar himself, albeit as a QB2. The Jets will likely have to throw the ball a lot again in Week 3 against the Detroit Lions, so Smith's projected high volume gives him top-16 upside in fantasy football.

metadata.title: Geno Smith steady in Week 2 loss
metadata.description: Geno Smith completed 27-of-41 pass attempts for 247 yards and one touchdown while also rushing five times for 17 yards in the Jets' 20-17 Week 2 loss to the Green Bay Packers.
metadata.analysis: Smith took what a strong Green Bay defense allowed Sunday, completing 65.9% of his passes in the loss. The veteran signal-caller will look to take advantage of a generous secondary in a favorable Week 3 matchup against the Detroit Lions.

metadata.title: Geno Smith - Struggles late in OT loss
metadata.description: Smith completed 27 of 41 passes for 247 yards and one touchdown in Sunday's 20-17 overtime loss to the Packers. He also rushed five times for 17 yards.
metadata.analysis: Smith navigated the Jets to a 17-7 lead with 11:04 remaining in the fourth quarter, but New York's offense stalled down the stretch, with a turnover on downs sandwiched around two punts on the team's final three possessions. Making his first home start for the Jets in nearly a decade, Smith threw his first touchdown pass of the season on a five-yard connection with Garrett Wilson in the third quarter. Smith hasn't turned the ball over but has just 462 passing yards heading into a Week 3 road game against the Lions, who allowed three touchdown passes apiece to Tyler Shough and Josh Allen.

metadata.title: Geno Smith a Low-End Option Against Green Bay
metadata.description: New York Jets quarterback Geno Smith did what the Jets needed in the opener. He completed 19 of 24 passes for 215 yards, did not turn the ball over, and was never sacked in the win over Tennessee. The problem for fantasy is that New York had little reason to ask much more of him. The Jets ran 39 times and controlled the game for long stretches, a formula they would probably be happy to use again on Sunday. Green Bay did allow three passing touchdowns last week, but Minnesota still finished with only 151 gross passing yards. Smith is QB27 in RotoBaller's Week 2 rankings. There could be a little more volume here if Green Bay pushes the score, but Smith is still much easier to use in Superflex than in a standard one-quarterback league.

metadata.title: Geno Smith Worth Monitoring On The Waiver Wire Early In The Season
metadata.description: New York Jets quarterback Geno Smith completed 19-of-24 passes for 215 yards with no touchdowns and rushed six times for seven yards in the team's Week 1 win over the Tennessee Titans. He showed good accuracy to begin the season but was not able to find a touchdown. Moving forward, Smith has some weapons in Garrett Wilson and Adonai Mitchell and once Omar Cooper, Jr. gets healthy. Smith is worth monitoring on the waiver wire as someone who can be a backup fantasy quarterback with some upside. He didn't have a huge game in Week 1, but he is capable in the Jets offense of producing fantasy relevant stats. Look for him to build off the accuracy he showed in the season opener and produce some more fruitful fantasy lines with more touchdowns up coming.

metadata.title: Geno Smith - Works as game manager in Week 1 win
metadata.description: Smith completed 19 of 24 passes for 215 yards while rushing six times for seven yards in Sunday's 23-10 win over the Titans.
metadata.analysis: Smith kept the offense on schedule but wasn't asked to do too much as the Jets rode their running game and defense to a convincing Week 1 win. There will likely be more pass-heavy game scripts to come, possibly as soon as Week 2 against the Packers, but Smith gave the Jets refreshingly competent quarterback play despite his modest yardage total to win the first game of his second stint with the team. Smith showed a nice connection with wide receivers Garrett Wilson and Adonai Mitchell, connecting with them on nine of 10 targets for 139 yards.

metadata.title: Geno Smith solid in Week 1 win over Titans
metadata.description: Geno Smith completed 19 of his 24 passes for 215 yards while adding seven yards on six carries in a 23-10 win over the Titans in Week 1.
metadata.analysis: It was a solid outing for the veteran quarterback in his return to the Jets. Smith did not throw any touchdowns in the win, but he also didn't turn the ball over and kept the chains moving. Smith will look to keep rolling as a low-end QB2 in fantasy heading into a Week 2 home matchup against the Packers.

metadata.title: Geno Smith Opens 2026 as a Superflex-Only Option
metadata.description: New York Jets quarterback Geno Smith begins his second stint with the franchise in Sunday's road opener against Tennessee. Smith is coming off a rough 2025 season with Las Vegas, where he threw for 3,025 yards, 19 touchdowns, and 17 interceptions in 15 starts while taking 55 sacks. New offensive coordinator Frank Reich and a healthy Garrett Wilson give him a better setup, but Tennessee's front can make his first start uncomfortable. Jeffery Simmons is coming off an 11-sack season, and the Titans recorded 42 sacks as a team in 2025. Smith also offers little rushing production to protect his fantasy floor after finishing last season without a rushing touchdown. RotoBaller has him at QB30 for Week 1. He should stay out of single-quarterback lineups and is best treated as a lower-end QB2 in Superflex formats.

metadata.title: Geno Smith a Deep-League Bounce-Back Candidate Entering 2026
metadata.description: New York Jets quarterback Geno Smith enters 2026 in search of a bounce-back season after a disastrous 2025 campaign. Across 15 games with the Las Vegas Raiders last year, Smith completed 67.4% of his pass attempts for 3,025 yards, 19 touchdowns, and 17 interceptions. As he enters his age-36 season, Smith may simply be past his prime. However, he was saddled with one of the worst offensive lines in football and a subpar group of healthy pass-catchers last season in Las Vegas. While the Jets enter 2026 with question marks on offense, Smith will have an exciting group of weapons to work with on offense in wide receivers Garrett Wilson and Adonai Mitchell, tight ends Mason Taylor and Kenyon Sadiq (groin), and running back Breece Hall (groin). In deeper leagues and two-quarterback formats, Smith could be worth targeting ahead of 2026.

metadata.title: Geno Smith - Voted team captain
metadata.description: Smith was voted a Jets captain by his teammates ahead of the 2026 season, Amanda Vogt and Eric Allen of the team's official site reports.
metadata.analysis: It's been nearly 10 years since Smith last took a snap for the Jets, but after revitalizing his career with the Seahawks and Raiders over the last four seasons, he's back in New York as a grizzled vet with age (34) and experience on his side. Smith recorded at least 3,000 yards and 19 touchdowns through the air in each of those four campaigns, but he also tossed 52 interceptions in 64 regular-season games during that span. Picks are often an issue for Smith, but he at least will have a nice skill-position group of RB Breece Hall (groin), WRs Garrett Wilson, Adonai Mitchell and Omar Cooper and TEs Mason Taylor and Kenyon Sadiq (abdomen) to throw to in 2026.
